arguments.query: Investigate current label sorting implementation and relevant tests. We must implement stable total ordering of heterogeneous labels: leading whitespace (never parsed, natural string order) first, then positive infinity, finite numeric, negative infinity, duration, bytes, semantic version, IP address, CIDR prefix, timestamp, untyped natural strings including empty and NaN. Typed ties use natural original strings. Numeric, duration and byte coefficients accept sign and scientific notation, reject bare exponent, and preserve arbitrary precision. Semver optional v and strict invalid fallback. IPv4 before IPv6, mapped IPv6 remains IPv6; CIDR equal network bytes smaller prefix first. Identify implementation location, reusable dependencies/parsers, test commands and any relevant instructions. Read-only investigation, only supplied checkout. Do not access other study directories or network.

report:
The relevant package is `model/labels`. There is no heterogeneous-value sorter currently. `Label` is just `{Name, Value string}`, and `Labels.New`/`FromStrings` sort only by label name. The three build variants (`stringlabels`, `slicelabels`, `dedupelabels`) each implement the same `Compare(Labels, Labels)` behavior: compare label names lexicographically, then values lexicographically, then shorter label sets first. Existing `Compare` is therefore the storage/series ordering primitive, not an appropriate place to introduce value-type ordering unless every caller is intentionally changed.

The existing tests cover only ordinary lexical label-set comparison, including value/name differences, prefixes, and empty sets. There are no tests for numeric, duration, byte, semver, IP, CIDR, timestamp, whitespace, NaN, or arbitrary-precision behavior. All current label package tests pass in the default, `slicelabels`, and `dedupelabels` variants:

- `go test ./model/labels` -> pass
- `go test -tags=slicelabels ./model/labels` -> pass
- `go test -tags=dedupelabels ./model/labels` -> pass

Relevant implementation implications:

- Add the heterogeneous comparator as a separate value/slice comparator in `model/labels`, or otherwise keep `Labels.Compare` unchanged unless the requested feature explicitly targets all series ordering. Many storage, query, remote-read, rule, and API paths call `labels.Compare` for canonical label-set ordering.
- The label package has three build-specific implementations, but a new ordinary package-level helper can be shared from a common file. If changing an existing method, all three variants need equivalent changes.
- The current Prometheus duration parser only accepts unsigned integer components with units ordered from years through milliseconds, has a `time.Duration` range limit, and its negative wrapper accepts only a leading minus. It does not accept decimal/scientific coefficients, so it cannot satisfy the requested duration grammar or arbitrary precision.
- `github.com/docker/go-units` is available transitively through Alertmanager, but its parser uses `strconv.ParseFloat`, rejects negative sizes, and converts to `int64`; it is unsuitable for signed scientific notation and arbitrary precision. `github.com/Masterminds/semver/v3` is also available transitively, and exposes `NewVersion` plus `StrictNewVersion`. It should not be assumed to be a direct dependency of this module without adding a direct requirement. Its normal `NewVersion` is explicitly semver-ish/coercing behavior, so strict fallback requirements need the strict parser or an explicit validation policy.
- `net/netip` is in the standard library and is already used elsewhere in the repository for `ParseAddr` and `ParsePrefix`. Its `Addr` family methods can support IPv4-before-IPv6 ordering, while mapped IPv6 should remain IPv6 by avoiding conversion through `Unmap`. `netip.Prefix` exposes prefix length and masked address data for CIDR comparison.
- `math/big`/`big.Rat` or a custom decimal representation is needed for exact signed/scientific numeric coefficients and to avoid float64 overflow/rounding. Bare exponents must be rejected before or during parsing. `strconv.ParseFloat` is not sufficient.

The canonical label-set ordering is consumed broadly, including matrix sorting and storage/index series ordering. In particular, the TSDB index writer compares incoming label sets with `labels.Compare` and rejects non-increasing series, so replacing that comparator with heterogeneous value semantics would alter on-disk/index invariants. A focused new test file under `model/labels` should exercise the requested total-order classes and comparator antisymmetry/transitivity, and should run under all three label build variants.
Investigation limitations:
- Source could not be attached: promql/value.go:314-71 (unavailable file or invalid range).

citations.reason: Defines Label as a name/value string pair, establishing where a heterogeneous value comparator would operate.
Shows stringlabels New/FromStrings sorting by name only and the common label construction path.
Shows the existing stringlabels Compare implementation, which compares encoded label names and values lexicographically.
Shows the slicelabels Compare implementation and its lexical name/value ordering.
Shows the dedupelabels Compare implementation and confirms the third build variant has the same lexical semantics.
Existing Compare tests cover only lexical names/values, prefixes, empty sets, and reverse ordering.
Storage merge ordering delegates to labels.Compare.
TSDB index series ordering uses labels.Compare, so changing it would affect index invariants.
The index writer rejects label sets that are not strictly increasing under labels.Compare.
External dependency source shows ParseDuration and ParseDurationAllowNegative limitations: integer-only components, ordered units, range limit, and leading-minus handling.
External dependency source shows byte parsing uses float64, rejects negatives, and converts to int64.
External semver dependency source documents NewVersion as semver-ish/coercing and shows its parse entry point.

arguments.query: Correction: target is PromQL sort_by_label and sort_by_label_desc in promql/functions.go around 642-690, which currently use facette/natsort. Please check relevant tests/harness and docs for these functions and suggest integration coverage. Do not investigate canonical model/labels further or external module source. Requirements same as previous query. Restrict evidence to supplied checkout. Return concise findings.

report:
The integration harness is already in place. `promql.TestEvaluations` calls `promqltest.RunBuiltinTests`, which embeds and runs every `promql/promqltest/testdata/*.test` file. The built-in parser enables experimental functions, so no harness change is needed.

`functions.test` already covers both functions with `expect ordered`: ascending and descending direction, multiple label-key precedence, full-label tie-breaking, numeric natural ordering (`0,1,2,3,10,11,12,20,21,100`), mixed alphanumeric values (`4m5,4m600,4m1000`), version-like values, NaN samples, and both float and histogram-compatible vectors. The existing expected ordering directly exercises the comparator in `promql/functions.go`.

Focused execution passed: `go test ./promql -run 'TestEvaluations/testdata/functions\\.test$' -count=1 -v`. The relevant subtests, including lines 754 through 881, passed. Running the full `TestEvaluations` also passed.

Recommended integration additions if the comparator implementation changes: add a small dedicated dataset with values that distinguish the intended natural-sort behavior, such as `item1`, `item2`, `item10`, and mixed digit/letter or leading-zero cases, and assert both ascending and descending results. Add cases where the requested label is absent, since `Metric.Get` supplies an empty value and this behavior is not explicitly isolated by the current tests. Add a range-query assertion only if needed to document that sorting does not affect range-result order, which the docs state is fixed. There is also an apparent duplicate ascending test at lines 767 and 780, both querying `sort_by_label(http_requests, "instance", "group")`; one should likely be replaced by a distinct tie/precedence case rather than copied.

The parser metadata marks both functions experimental and variadic, so parser-level registration is already covered by `TestFunctionList`; implementation-level behavior belongs in `promql/promqltest/testdata/functions.test`.
